candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — comfort measures, mobility and postoperative care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — postoperative pulmonary hygiene and comfort
candidate.educational_objective: Use pain control and coached pulmonary-hygiene measures to improve lung expansion and secretion clearance after surgery.

options.A: Encourage prescribed pain-control measures, then coach deep breathing and coughing while the client splints the incision as appropriate
options.B: Ask the client to avoid coughing and deep breathing until the incision is pain free so the wound is not stressed
options.C: Keep the client on strict bed rest because mobility and deeper respirations increase the risk of atelectasis
options.D: Use leg exercises as the primary intervention for lung expansion and secretion clearance

candidate.rationale: Postoperative pulmonary care includes adequate pain control plus deep breathing/coughing and other prescribed lung-expansion measures. Splinting can reduce incisional discomfort during coughing. These measures promote ventilation and secretion clearance and reduce atelectasis risk; they complement, rather than replace, mobilization and other prescribed prophylaxis.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Postoperative respiratory care uses lung-expansion/secretion-clearance measures, with splinting and pain management supporting participation.
candidate.source_locator: Table 2.5b Routine Postoperative Nursing Interventions — respiratory care: teach coughing/deep breathing or prescribed incentive spirometry; teach splinting; ambulate to promote ventilation and secretion removal
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
candidate.stem: A postoperative client is taking shallow breaths because movement of the abdominal incision is painful. Which nursing intervention best supports prevention of postoperative pulmonary complications?
